primitives.name: Quantile Tracker
primitives.verbatim_quote: Basic quantile tracker: q_{t+1} = q_t + η(err_t - α) (this is ACI in score space).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'q_t': 'quantile level, dimensionless', 'η': 'learning rate, positive scalar', 'err_t': 'prediction error at time t, dimensionless', 'α': 'target coverage level, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Error process is bounded; learning rate η > 0.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Unstable convergence when η too large or errors unbounded.

layer2.mapping: Maps prediction errors directly into quantile adjustments, forming the basis of integral control in PID framework.
layer2.telemetry: Running empirical coverage deviation from nominal α.

primitives.name: General Controller
primitives.verbatim_quote: General controller: q_{t+1} = q̂_{t+1} + r_t(Σ_i (err_i - α)), where q̂_{t+1} is the **scorecaster** (any forecaster predicting the next score from observable features — e.g., Theta, or a model on cases/deaths) and r_t is a **saturating integrator** (e.g., tan-based saturation) applied to cumulative errors.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{q}_{t+1}': 'predicted score from scorecaster, dimensionless', 'r_t': 'saturating integrator function, bounded scalar', 'err_i': 'error at time i, dimensionless', 'α': 'target coverage level, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Scorecaster predicts future scores; integrator r_t is bounded and saturates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when scorecaster is inaccurate or integrator fails to saturate.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a full PID controller where the scorecaster acts as derivative term and the integrator as I-term.
layer2.telemetry: Long-run coverage error and interval width stability.

primitives.name: Scorecaster
primitives.verbatim_quote: The P term reacts instantly to misses; the I term kills persistent bias; the scorecaster anticipates.
primitives.assumptions: Observable features predict future score behavior accurately.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Anticipation fails when feature signals are noisy or absent.

layer2.mapping: Provides predictive input to the controller, enabling anticipation of predictable miscoverage.
layer2.telemetry: Forecast accuracy of score predictions against actual errors.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of conformal PID control lies in its decomposition of coverage control into three distinct feedback mechanisms: proportional (P), integral (I), and derivative-like (D) components. The P term ensures rapid adjustment to current prediction errors, making it suitable for handling sudden shocks such as those seen in the December weather or post-bye chaos. The I term corrects for persistent biases by accumulating past errors through a saturating integrator, ensuring long-run coverage stability even under distributional shifts. The scorecaster component provides a predictive signal that allows the system to anticipate predictable miscoverage patterns—such as seasonal trends or known event impacts—by modeling future score sequences based on observable features. This architecture subsumes ACI (the I-only controller) as a special case while adding robustness through P and D terms. The theoretical guarantee of deterministic long-run coverage arises from bounding the error accumulation and ensuring that the scorecaster and integrator satisfy specific boundedness conditions. In practice, this enables GSE to maintain stable coverage levels during volatile regimes without relying on stochastic assumptions.
